Users

Field Actions

The treatment actions crew picks from in the field app. Each action can require medications, require a note, count as a death event, or be once-per-animal.

Field Protocols

Default medications per action. Set a global default (applies to all lots), or override per lot. When crew picks an action in the field app, meds auto-fill from the matching protocol.

Data tools

Helpers for keeping the data clean. Use carefully — these run real deletes.

Test lots cleanup

Removes all lots with names starting with TEST_ or TEST-, including their invoices, load-outs, doctoring events, deaths, sales, and pasture assignments. Field protocols seeded for testing also get removed.

Lots missing invoices

Active lots with no invoices entered yet. Head_in shows 0 (or negative if there are deaths) until invoices are added.

Doctoring Entry

One protocol per batch. Type a tag, press Enter → row appends with lot, weight, and computed doses. Click any cell to edit. Save commits the whole batch. After save, action/date stay so you can immediately start the next protocol.

Where these animals were worked. Picking here sets every row at once; each row can then be changed on its own. Feeds the field app's tag lookup.
Pick an action first, then start adding tags.

Single Doctoring

One-off doctoring event entry. Type a tag → lot auto-resolves. For NT animals, check the box and pick the lot. Opens the standard doctoring modal pre-filled with lot context.

Type tag and press Enter to identify the lot and open the doctoring modal.

Doctoring search

Search across all lots in the current fiscal year. Click any result to edit.

Searches all fiscal years but only open lots by default, so a tag finds the current animal. Tag numbers reused in later years won't collide because old lots are closed. Check "Include closed lots" to search history (tag numbers may repeat across years — use the Lot and Date columns to tell them apart).

Type a tag number, pick an action, or pick a lot to search.

Fresh Cattle — Doctoring Eligibility

Receipts within 17 days of receiving on open lots, by in-date, tag range, and pasture. Loads drop off automatically after day 17. "OK to pull" = in-date + 8 days (Draxxin post-metaphylaxis window; day 9 in parentheses).

Deaths by days on feed (DOF)

When in a lot's life are deaths happening? Helps identify whether early-arrival stress, mid-period BRD, or late-stage issues drive losses. Calculated using each death's date minus the lot's arrival date. Anonymous bulk-entered deaths use that event's date as a single point — accurate enough at the cohort level.

One row per buyer settlement sheet. A shipment can span any number of lots and pastures; the sheet's totals are allocated down to each of them.

Move cattle

One ticket per move. Work through as many lots and pastures as you like — the counts walk down as you go, so a pasture you draw on twice shows what is actually left. Nothing is written until you save, and if any ticket fails the whole batch is put back.

Recent moves

Loading…

Needs attention

Everything outstanding across feed and meds in one place — what is late, what arrived without a ticket, what has not been billed, and what does not tie. Rows appear because a field is empty, not because somebody remembered to write a note, and they clear themselves when the number is typed.

Loading…

Orders

An order is optional — a load that arrives unannounced is still recordable, and shows on the list as unordered. What an order buys you is the price: a delivery against one is costed the moment it lands, so the feed never reads free while the bill is in the post. A line with no quantity is a reminder; it closes itself when a delivery of that item arrives.

Loading…

Invoices

Type the bill once and tick the loads it covers. If the total agrees with what those loads were expected to cost — and it usually will — you are done in one click. If it does not, the difference is spread and the part already fed is booked to price variance; costs already frozen onto feed that has been eaten are never rewritten. Redwing still owns the payable: this records only enough to reconcile inventory cost.

Loading…

Medication inventory

The ordering spine already carries meds — an order line, a bill and the paperwork worklist all take a medication today. What is not built yet is the stock ledger: how many bottles are on hand, and therefore what counts as low.

Until then the medication catalog stays where it is, under Animal Health → Medications. One drug, two screens, two different questions: what it is and how it is dosed there, how much of it we have here.

Feed on hand

FIFO layers, valued at what each load actually cost delivered. Pounds sitting on a load that has not been priced yet are counted but not valued — they show in the Unpriced column rather than being quietly worth zero.

Loading…

Deliveries

One row per load delivered. Pick the open order it came against and the item, bay, vendor and price fill themselves in. Freight belongs in the cost — a delivered $/ton is the only number that means anything, and pulling freight out makes every lot's feed read low. A load cannot be deleted once any of its pounds have been fed out.

Loading…

Feed out

Recent feed-out

Loading…

Physical counts

Sacks are counted; bays are estimated. Which one it was is recorded on the line, because a −4,000 lb variance on an estimated bay is Tuesday and the same variance on counted sacks is a keying error or a theft. Posting a count writes real ledger rows: short of book becomes shrink, over book becomes found feed at the last known price.

Loading…

Mix a batch

A premix is several commodities mixed into one, stored in its own bay and fed over the following days. The ingredients are consumed at their own FIFO prices and the dollars become the premix's price — so once it is mixed, the premix behaves like any other item. Feed the premix, never the premix and its ingredients, or the same feed is counted twice.

Loading…

Recipes

A recipe pre-fills the batch screen and nothing more. What actually goes in the mixer is what gets saved and priced, so editing a recipe never changes what a past batch was made of.

Loading…

Feed cost by lot

Every feed-out is spread across the head-days inside its own period, so a week's corn lands on the days the cattle actually ate it. Head-days come from arrivals by receipt date — cattle eat from the day they hit the ground.

Loading…

Feed that could not be charged to a day

Real dollars against a lot that had no cattle standing inside the period entered. Usually a period typed before the lot arrived, after it shipped, or running past today. Shown here rather than silently dropped.

Loading…

Post to Redwing

to

One week of feed becomes four postings. Each section below is laid out in the order of the Redwing screen it is typed into, so it is read straight down. Pounds and dollars are the app’s — the app is the system of record for feed on hand, and Redwing receives its dollars.

Pick a period and press Run.

Feed items

There is no price here on purpose. Price lives on the load that brought it in and freezes when the feed is used, so editing a price can never rewrite a closed lot. That is the opposite of how medications behave, and it is deliberate.

Loading…

Storage locations

Somewhere feed is stored and counted — a bay, a barn, a pallet of sacks. Bulk feeders standing in pastures are not locations; feed leaving a bay for a feeder is just feed-out. Deactivate rather than delete once a bay has held anything, so its history survives.

Loading…

Accounting Report

One shipment, one row per lot and pasture, in the column order your accounting software expects. Head, pay weight and dollars are the shipment's own allocation, so the rows add back to the draft exactly.

These three are remembered for next time. Production Center is printed as the lot number exactly as the app holds it — translate it as you key the entry if your software wants a different code.

Pick a shipment.

Loads & weight groups

A group is a class of cattle that shipped at one average weight. Enter each truckload with the lot and pasture it was gathered off — that is also how the cattle come out of their pastures, so there is nothing else to fill in. Pick the lot or the pasture first, whichever you know; each one narrows the other. A pasture holding more than one lot says so, and a load drawn off it takes a line per lot.

Enter what you actually counted. The books’ split is an estimate carried forward from earlier moves — this replaces it with the count and records the moves that make the change honest.

Correct field entry

Nothing here is in the books yet — this only changes what will be posted when the entry is approved. The cowboy’s original entry is kept.

Edit shipment — money only

Loads, head, weights, lots, pastures and dates are not touched — changing those would unwind head math that has already happened. Everything here is money, so the allocation is simply recomputed over the loads already recorded and no cattle move.

Shrink & counts

A premix going short means the batch was never recorded and its ingredients are still on the books. It gets its own line on Anomalies rather than the ordinary short flag.

Delivery

Choosing an open order line fills in the rest and costs this load at the agreed price.

Quantity

Type either one and the other fills in.
Gross × (1 − allowance) becomes the booked pounds above and carries the full cost, so the price per pound rises on day one and every pound fed carries its share. Gross is kept so next season’s allowance calibrates against it, never against the booked figure.

Cost

Freight goes in the cost, not beside it. This is the price this feed carries for the rest of its life — it freezes onto every pound when the feed is used.

Type either one and the other fills in. Tickets quote a rate; invoices quote a total.
Deliberate and visible, rather than saving a blank that would quietly make this feed free. Feed can still be used against it; the cost fills in when you price it.
The needs-attention list chases a missing ticket or bill because the field is empty. Tick this for the load where nothing more is coming — it stops the chasing and records who decided that. Typing the ticket number clears it on its own.
